questions.prompt: A delivery robot drives along a flat floor at a constant 2 m/s. What is the net force on it?
options: Equal to the drive force alone
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means zero acceleration, so the net force is zero: drive balances friction and drag. A large velocity does not need a net force.

questions.prompt: A 4 kg cart has drive u = 10 N and viscous drag c = 2 kg/s. At v = 3 m/s what is its acceleration in m/s^2? Give 2 decimals.
What is the kinetic energy (in J) of the 4 kg cart moving at 3 m/s? Give 1 decimal.
In m dv/dt = u - c v, what are the SI units of c?
questions.explanation: c v must be a force (N = kg m/s^2); with v in m/s, c is kg/s.

questions.prompt: A cart starts from rest and accelerates at a constant 1.5 m/s^2 for 5 s. How far does it travel, in metres? Give 2 decimals.
A cart is driven by a constant 12 N against viscous drag c = 3 kg/s. What is its terminal speed in m/s? Give 1 decimal.
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity u = c v, so v = 12/3 = 4 m/s.

questions.prompt: Explicit Euler for m dv/dt = -c v is stable and non-oscillating only if c dt/m < 1, and energy-decreasing if c dt/m < 2. For m = 5 kg and c = 2 kg/s, what is the largest dt (in seconds) for which kinetic energy is guaranteed to decrease each step? Give 1 decimal.
questions.explanation: The factor 1 - c dt/m must satisfy |.| < 1, i.e. dt < 2m/c = 5 s.

questions.prompt: A cart coasts with its motor off. Its speed halves every 3 s regardless of the starting speed. Which friction model fits?
options: No friction; the motor is still driving
Quadratic drag proportional to velocity squared
questions.explanation: A fixed fraction lost per fixed time is exponential decay: viscous drag. Coulomb friction removes a fixed amount of speed per time, and quadratic drag slows fast motion more.

questions.prompt: A robot's wheels have friction coefficient 0.35 against a ramp. What is the steepest angle (degrees) it can hold without sliding? Give 1 decimal.
questions.explanation: tan(theta) = mu, theta = atan(0.35) = 19.3 degrees. Mass cancels.

questions.prompt: At the terminal velocity of the driven cart, which statement about power is correct?
options: Kinetic energy is increasing at rate u v
Drive power equals power dissipated by drag
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is constant, so u v = c v^2: the drive power equals the dissipated power.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg robot is driven up a 10 degree ramp by a wheel force F. Describe the free-body diagram, the axes and sign convention you choose, and the equation of motion along the ramp.
rubric: Lists the forces on the robot only: weight mg, normal force perpendicular to the ramp, drive/friction force along the ramp (and drag if modelled)
Chooses axes along and perpendicular to the ramp and states the positive direction
Writes m a = F - m g sin(10 deg) - drag along the ramp, with N = m g cos(10 deg) perpendicular
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Your coast-down simulation of a cart looks plausible but you suspect an error. Name two physical checks you can code and what each would reveal.
rubric: Kinetic energy must not increase when the motor is off (catches a sign error or too large a time step)
Comparison with the closed form v0*exp(-c t/m) and halving the step to see the error halve (catches order/step problems)
Mentions units or terminal velocity u/c as a further check
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
